title: Summary: Church witness proves Scripture — it is not a higher rule of faith
source_text: XLIV. In summa ergo fatemur authoritatem librorum sacrorum per Ecclesiae consensum & testimonium recte & valide probari. Sed negamus tamen inde sequi quod adversarii volunt, nempe Ecclesiae testimonium esse regulam fidei Scriptura ipsa notiorem quoad nos. Non enim omnis bona probatio ex aliqua fidei regula & principio sumitur, nec etiam ex eo quod est simpliciter notius & certius: sed saepe res probare cogimur ad hominem, & a posteriori.
pass_a_gloss: In sum, therefore, we confess that the authority of the sacred books is rightly and validly proved through the consensus and testimony of the Church. But we deny nevertheless that what the adversaries want follows from this — namely that the testimony of the Church is a rule of faith better known as regards us than Scripture itself. For not every good proof is taken from some rule and principle of faith, nor even from that which is simply better known and more certain: but often we are compelled to prove a matter to the man, and a posteriori.
pass_b_english: In short, then: we grant that the sacred books' authority is rightly and validly proved by the Church's consensus and testimony.
We deny what the adversaries infer — that the Church's testimony is a rule of faith better known to us than Scripture itself.
Not every sound proof is taken from a rule and principle of faith, or even from what is simply better known and more certain. Often we must prove the point to the person before us, and a posteriori.

choices.why: Opponent-relative proof, not modern insult sense.
